newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices recover as fund buyers return to market.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices recover as fund buyers return to market.

text.p: World oil prices recovered in late trade on Wednesday as fund buying resumed, supported by concern at forecasts that the United States is set to endure its coldest winter spell later this week, traders and analysts said.

London February futures for international benchmark North Sea Brent blend traded in over a one dollar range on Wednesday ending the day 30 cents off the high, but up 44 cents on the day, at $23.80 a barrel.
It flirted with its six-year high of $25.06 last week when it reached $24.91, but since then has shed over a dollar as the funds locked in their profits.
The colder U.S. weather and an inventory report on Tuesday showing another drop in U.S. home heating oil supplies may cushion further declines, analysts said.
"You definitely saw the funds get in at the beginning of the year and get out a week later," said Peter Gignoux, manager of Smith Barney's petroleum desk in London.
"I think they certainly are worried about the cold weather but you had a New Year's rally full of exuberance and that rally has corrected itself.
"The fact remains that PADD one heating oil stocks are substantially lower than last year and we drew again," he said. "I think I have to be bullish. Winter isn't over-- we've barely gotten into it."

American Petroleum Institute said distillate stocks in the Northeast U.S., or PADD one, which is the world's largest region for heating oil demand, fell 419,000 barrels to 46.8 million and were still 2.8 million under a year ago.
Total distillate supplies fell 1.3 million barrels while gasoline stocks rose a meagre 415,000 barrels and stood at a 9.3 million barrel deficit to its year ago levels.
"Prices have been remarkably resilient," Gignoux said. "Weather and stocks -- that's the key."

Private forecaster Weather Services Corp predicted that Arctic air would move from the Midwest into the Northeast U.S. through the weekend, when prices will drop to 15-30 degrees Fahrenheit below normal.
Gignoux added that oil prices were lightly supported by lingering concerns over the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin. Russia is a major producer and exporter of oil.
Yeltsin, who had a quintuple bypass operation on November 5 and is suffering from pneumonia, must stay in hospital until the end of this week.
Chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov said Yeltsin's condition has "stabilised significantly" in the past three days but that complications from the pneumonia were possible.
